summary: This document changes the "Unassigned" number space in the IANA OSPFv3 Instance ID Address Family Values registry by splitting it in two. One half stays unassigned, managed via Standards Action, and the other is reserved for private use. It updates RFC 5838.

eli5.summary: A list of open numbers is cut in half. One half is kept for official use and the other for anyone's private use.

questions: what are ospfv3 private use instance ids
subtitle: Carves a block of OSPFv3 Instance IDs out for private use.

tldr.problem: Operators sometimes need extra OSPFv3 instances to identify specific applications, but the Instance ID registry had no range they could assign locally.
tldr.mechanism: Instance IDs 192-255 are designated Reserved for Private Use, and the remaining unassigned values 128-191 require Standards Action.
tldr.outcome: Operators get a pool of IDs to assign locally, and the registry reference to RFC 5838 is removed for the modified ranges.

today: RFC 6969 is a Proposed Standard from July 2013 that updates RFC 5838. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 5838 defined the "OSPFv3 Instance ID Address Family Values" registry, which maps OSPFv3 Instance IDs to address families. Values 0 to 127 are allocated there (for example 0 is IPv6 unicast, 32 is base IPv6 multicast, 64 is base IPv4 unicast and 96 is base IPv4 multicast), and 128-255 were unassigned.

Some networks need additional OSPFv3 instances to operationally identify specific applications. One example is a draft that carries IPv4 packets over an IPv6 network using IPv4-embedded IPv6 addresses, where a separate Instance ID space would help identify the application.
sections.eli5: Sometimes a network wants its own labels for its own jobs. It needs a set of numbers it can hand out itself.

sections.title: The Registry Update
sections.content: Instance IDs 192-255 are now Reserved for Private Use under RFC 5226. The remaining unassigned values, 128-191, are assigned by Standards Action.
sections.eli5: The last quarter of the list is for anyone to use. The middle part stays open for official rules.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content: IANA modified the registry as described, and removed the reference to RFC 5838 for the modified ranges. The document says it introduces no new security issues.
sections.eli5: It only relabels numbers, so nothing new is risky.
